name: Amazon S3
sku: Amazon S3 general purpose buckets and S3 Tables table buckets.

store.object-store.note: An object storage service for any amount of data, used for data lakes, backup, archive and big data analytics.

store.table-format.note: S3 Tables are a separate bucket type that stores tables in Apache Iceberg format and runs compaction, snapshot management and unreferenced-file cleanup automatically. It is one bucket type among four, not what S3 is mainly used for.

source.file-drop.note: Files are uploaded into buckets and picked up from there, which is how partner extracts and exports commonly land. SFTP delivery needs AWS Transfer Family, a separate service.

bands.note: Buckets are private by default, with access managed through IAM, bucket policies, access points and Block Public Access. Control is at bucket, prefix or object-tag level, not column or row level.
Object Lock enforces write-once-read-many retention with retention periods and legal holds, and lifecycle rules transition or expire objects.
CloudWatch metrics track the operational health of S3 resources and CloudTrail records bucket and object API calls. This is service health and access auditing, not data freshness.

presentation.tagline: Object storage that underpins most AWS data lakes.

cost.note: S3 Standard storage, us-east-1, genuinely tiered: $0.023/GB for the first 50TB, $0.022/GB up to 500TB, $0.021/GB above that. Each point also assumes a plausible amount of request and egress traffic for a pipeline storing that much (PUT/COPY/POST/LIST $0.005/1,000 requests, GET/SELECT $0.0004/1,000, egress free for the first 100GB/month then tiered from $0.09/GB down) — stated per point, not billed at a flat rate.
